paragraphs: RUN is KAIST's algorithmic problem solving club.
Every semester, we grow our problem-solving skills together through study sessions and contests.

study.title: Study Sessions
study.body: RUN holds regular study sessions. Each member can choose to join the Beginner, Intermediate, or Advanced track.

levels.name: Beginner
levels.description: Learn the fundamental techniques of problem solving.

levels.name: Advanced
levels.description: Focus on contest preparation and practical problem solving.

contests.title: Contest Participation
contests.body: RUN has consistently achieved excellent results by participating in a variety of programming contests.

list.name: ICPC
list.description: RUN's primary goal contest, held every fall.

list.name: UCPC
list.fullName: Union of Clubs for Programming Contests
list.description: A nationwide team contest organized jointly by Korean university programming clubs, held every summer.

list.name: SCPC
list.description: An algorithmic programming contest for university students hosted by Samsung.

list.name: Codeforces
list.description: One of the world's most popular online competitive programming platforms, with regular rated contests.

list.name: AtCoder
list.description: A Japanese online competitive programming platform hosting contests of various levels every week.

hosting.title: Contest Hosting
hosting.body: RUN members write the problems themselves to host these contests.
hosting.photoAlt: Photo from a past contest venue (coming soon)

events.name: KAIST RUN Spring Contest
events.description: A chance to test the skills you've honed through club activities.

events.name: KAIST ICPC Mock Competition
events.description: A campus mock competition held ahead of the real ICPC.

recruit.line1: Anyone who enjoys algorithmic problem solving

archive.title: Contest Archive
archive.description: These are the competitions hosted by RUN.
